sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. April 23 announcement and April 24 API update explicitly name GPT-5.5 Pro. Its exact Pro comparison columns report performance; inference-efficiency discussion and more-compute language give no nominal total or active parameter count.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 Pro API model documentation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 through official OpenAI documentation and fresh full Markdown. Exact gpt-5.5-pro-2026-04-23 model uses more compute and supports medium/high(default)/xhigh reasoning effort, 1,050,000 context, 128,000 output, text/image input, text output, Responses, Batch and function calling. No total or active model-size specification is present; API request parameters and context limits are different quantities.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 from fresh HTTP-200 full PDF/text. Section 1 explicitly calls GPT-5.5 Pro the same underlying GPT-5.5 model using parallel test-time compute. This is an explicit unchanged-model relationship rather than pruning, distillation, expert expansion or a new-modality model, but the underlying model has no disclosed nominal count to inherit. Section 2 and complete-text parameter/count searches supply neither total nor active parameters.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 from fresh HTTP-200 full PDF/text. Later July 9 system card Tables 2 and 3 explicitly include gpt-5.5-pro, reporting protein-binding pass@4 and DNA-design pass@1. These are benchmark scores, not active-parameter columns. Full-text review found no total or active size for the exact Pro model; NanoGPT tasks concern separately trained small models.

sources.title: GeneBench: Assessing AI Agents for Multi-Stage Inference Problems in Genomics and Quantitative Biology
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 from fresh HTTP-200 full PDF/text. Results and Supplementary Table 2 explicitly report GPT-5.5 Pro in the separate Pro harness, including 33.2% pass rate. Columns cover success rates, regimes, token use and replicate counts, not model parameters. Scientific data-generating parameters elsewhere are unrelated to production model size.

sources.title: Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.5
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 from fresh HTTP-200 full PDF/text. July 29 summary names underlying GPT-5.5, explicitly says it is not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model, and gives training-data quantities rather than model size. The original system card binds Pro to that underlying model, but neither document supplies a nominal count or a counted prior base.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Current guide explicitly names GPT-5.5 Pro in its model-differences table and gpt-5.5-pro in the extended-retention support list. It explains KV tensors. This binds caching to the exact Pro variant despite its lack of a cached-input discount.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: The archived guide explicitly applies before GPT-5.6 and explains OpenAI caching through Transformer attention key/value projections. Together with the exact Pro caching binding, it supports a qualified broad Transformer inference; it does not disclose full block structure or dense/MoE layout.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses accepts PDF files. For vision-capable models, PDFs are converted to extracted text and page images. Combined with exact Pro vision and Responses support, this establishes PDF as an API input format rather than an additional native sensory modality.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: April 24, 2026 entry explicitly releases GPT-5.5 Pro for Responses API requests. This follows April 23 ChatGPT availability and does not change the dated April 23 model snapshot.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The complete current document was checked for exact gpt-5.5-pro and its dated identifier; no API shutdown notice was found. This is a documentation observation, not an endpoint availability test.

sources.title: Model Release Notes
sources.evidence: The October 14, 2026 GPT-5.5 product-retirement notice covers ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex and explicitly says API access is unaffected. The notice does not separately enumerate Pro; it is not used to assert an exact Pro API shutdown.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited nonexclusive service/API use and reserve service IP. Combined with hosted distribution, this supports descriptive proprietary licensing, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: Official inventory lists GPT-5.5 Pro as a hosted model and separately lists gpt-oss-120b/20b as Apache-licensed open-weight models. Checked release and model pages offer no downloadable Pro weights.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 API model documentation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 in fresh full Markdown. Underlying GPT-5.5 documentation supplies interface/capability limits and prompt_caching, but no nominal total or active parameter count. The original card explicitly binds Pro to this same model; no count can be inferred from the relationship without a supported base-model count.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-5.5 Pro record
sources.evidence: The original catalog lead was accessed through its raw file and checked against primary sources. Its derived-looking 922K input limit is not adopted without an explicit primary limit.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 HTTP-200 PDF and complete extracted text inspected; web rendering separately rejected the 15.8 MB file. September 3 card Tables 16 and 17 explicitly name gpt-5.5-pro and report protein-binding/DNA-design scores. Neither these tables nor the full-document parameter search supplies a nominal total or activated count for Pro.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 — Inference Specs & Pricing
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 as a rejected secondary search lead. Page asserts underlying GPT-5.5 has 700B total/110B active and detailed MoE dimensions without a supporting original model-team parameter disclosure. The visible verification link is to OpenRouter, while the page mixes these claims with hypothetical self-hosting estimates. It does not establish GPT-5.5 or Pro specifications.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review of original release/card/API sources and later exact-Pro comparisons found no nominal total. Explicit same-underlying-GPT-5.5 lineage passes the structural-change check, but that base has no supported count to inherit. The EU summary also rules out prior-model fine-tune lineage. Bounded later-disclosure and research-team comparison searches found no original count; unsupported secondary 700B is not adopted.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh independent search for active/activated-parameter disclosures and original model-team tables found no count for exact GPT-5.5 Pro. Later GPT-5.6/Astra tables and GeneBench report task scores or usage, not activated model size. Parallel test-time compute does not specify active weights or MoE topology. Unsupported secondary 110B is rejected; no dense total=active inference is made.

The original same-underlying-model relation independently connects Pro to GPT-5.5. Detailed blocks, dense/MoE topology and counts remain undisclosed; no pricing discount is needed for this structural inference.

context_window.note: Exact API total context is 1,050,000 tokens with 128,000 maximum output. Do not derive a separate maximum-input ceiling by subtraction or transfer Codex product limits. No live endpoint test was performed.

modalities.note: Native text/image input and text output. PDF is retained as an API document format converted into text and page images. Hosted image-generation tools and audio/video training data are not native Pro output/input modalities.

reasoning.note: Exact Pro document supports reasoning tokens with medium, high(default) and xhigh effort. Parallel test-time compute is explicitly documented.

tool_call.note: Exact model supports function calling and Responses tools. Batch support is documented. Built-in computer use, tool search, apply_patch and skills are not transferred from GPT-5.5.

Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.5

patch.notes: Released in ChatGPT April 23, 2026; API availability followed April 24. Default API snapshot is gpt-5.5-pro-2026-04-23. Context is 1,050,000 tokens with 128,000 maximum output; reasoning supports medium, high(default) and xhigh. PDF denotes API extraction into text and page images. The system card identifies Pro as the same underlying GPT-5.5 model with parallel test-time compute. Transformer is a qualified broad inference from exact Pro prompt-caching documentation and the pre-GPT-5.6 KV mechanism, corroborated by that model relationship; detailed topology and total/active counts remain undisclosed. The same-model relationship supplies no size because GPT-5.5 has no supported count; additional test-time compute and later benchmark scores do not establish parameters. The GPT-5.5 October 14 product-retirement notice explicitly excludes API access and does not separately enumerate Pro. No exact Pro API shutdown notice was found; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter-only re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts after reopening original sources, the underlying-model training summary, GeneBench and later exact-Pro comparisons through GPT-6 Astra. Pro is explicitly the same underlying GPT-5.5 model, but no supported base count exists to inherit. Bounded later-disclosure and original active-count-table searches found no acceptable number; unsupported secondary counts are rejected. Explicit null patches include both counts and parameters_source. The other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
